title: New Health Standards Reveal Higher Dementia Risks
subtitle: A broader way to define obesity shows that many more people may be at risk for brain health issues than previously thought.

summary.en: Recent research suggests that traditional methods for measuring obesity are no longer enough to understand health risks. A new study shows that using a broader definition of obesity helps identify more people at risk of dementia. This method considers body fat distribution and other health conditions rather than just weight. Researchers found that over 80% of people previously labeled as overweight actually fit the new criteria for obesity. These findings could change how doctors monitor brain health in older adults.
summary.zh: 近期研究顯示，傳統衡量肥胖的方法已不足以了解健康風險。一項新研究表明，採用更廣泛的肥胖定義有助於識別更多失智症高風險族群。這種方法考量了體脂肪分佈與其他健康狀況，而不僅僅是體重。研究人員發現，超過百分之八十先前被標記為過重的人，實際上符合新的肥胖標準。這些發現可能會改變醫師監測老年人腦部健康的方式。

paragraphs.en: Following our recent report on how we measure body health, new data has provided a clearer look at the link between obesity and dementia. For a long time, doctors have used Body Mass Index, or BMI, to decide if someone has obesity. BMI is a simple calculation based on a person’s height and weight. However, many experts now believe this method is too simple. A new study published in the journal Neurology suggests that a more detailed approach is necessary to truly understand the risks of dementia—a group of conditions that cause a decline in memory and thinking skills.
paragraphs.zh: 繼我們近期報導關於如何衡量身體健康狀況後，新數據讓我們能更清晰地了解肥胖與失智症之間的關聯。長期以來，醫師一直使用身體質量指數（BMI）來判定一個人是否肥胖。身體質量指數是根據身高與體重計算出的簡單數值。然而，許多專家現在認為這種方法過於簡化。一項發表在《神經學》（Neurology）期刊上的新研究指出，若要真正了解失智症的風險，必須採取更細緻的評估方式；失智症是一組導致記憶力與思考能力衰退的症狀總稱。

paragraphs.en: According to MedPage Today, researchers led by Rui Zhou from Guangdong Pharmaceutical University in China have tested a different framework created by the European Association for the Study of Obesity, or EASO. Unlike the traditional BMI method, the EASO system looks at three different factors: BMI, where body fat is stored, and other existing health problems. These health problems, known as comorbidities—or the presence of two or more diseases in the same person at the same time—can include issues like heart disease or diabetes. By looking at the whole picture, the EASO framework provides a more complete view of a person’s health.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《今日醫學頁》（MedPage Today）報導，由中國廣東藥科大學的周瑞（Rui Zhou）所領導的研究團隊，測試了一套由歐洲肥胖研究協會（EASO）所建立的全新評估架構。與傳統的身體質量指數法不同，歐洲肥胖研究協會的系統考量了三個不同因素：身體質量指數、脂肪在體內的堆積位置，以及其他既有的健康問題。這些被稱為共病症的健康問題，指的是同一個人同時患有兩種或多種疾病，例如心臟病或糖尿病。透過審視整體狀況，這套架構能提供更全面的個人健康觀點。

paragraphs.en: The study analyzed information from over 17,000 people in England and China. The results were striking. When researchers applied the EASO rules to the participants, they found that more than 80% of people who were previously labeled as just 'overweight' were actually in the 'obesity' category. This shift suggests that millions of people who thought they were at a moderate health risk might actually face a much higher danger of developing dementia later in life.
paragraphs.zh: 該研究分析了來自英國與中國超過一萬七千人的資訊，結果相當驚人。當研究人員將歐洲肥胖研究協會的標準套用到參與者身上時，他們發現超過百分之八十原本僅被標記為「過重」的人，實際上已達到「肥胖」的標準。這項轉變顯示，數百萬原本以為自己僅處於中度健康風險的人，在晚年罹患失智症的風險可能遠比想像中高。

paragraphs.en: MedPage Today noted that the study found people who met the EASO definition of obesity had double the risk of dementia compared to those with a normal weight and no other health issues. Conversely, the study found that those who were classified as 'overweight' under the new system actually had a lower risk of dementia than those with normal weight. This surprising result shows just how much our current definitions of health need to be updated to be more accurate.
paragraphs.zh: 《今日醫學頁》指出，研究發現符合歐洲肥胖研究協會肥胖定義的人，其罹患失智症的風險是體重正常且無其他健康問題者的兩倍。相反地，研究發現那些在新系統下被歸類為「過重」的人，其失智症風險反而比體重正常者更低。這項令人驚訝的結果顯示，我們現行的健康定義需要進行多大的更新，才能達到更精確的程度。

paragraphs.en: Why does this matter for the brain? Experts explain that obesity can harm the brain in several ways. It can cause inflammation, which is the body’s way of reacting to injury or stress, and it can also damage the blood vessels that supply the brain. These changes can specifically target areas of the brain responsible for memory and decision-making. By identifying these risks earlier, doctors hope they can help patients make lifestyle changes that protect their long-term brain health.
paragraphs.zh: 為什麼這對大腦很重要？專家解釋，肥胖會以多種方式損害大腦。它會引發發炎反應，這是身體對損傷或壓力所產生的反應，同時也會損害供應大腦的血管。這些變化可能特別針對大腦中負責記憶與決策的區域。透過更早識別出這些風險，醫師希望能協助病患改變生活型態，進而保護長期的腦部健康。

paragraphs.en: This is not the first time the traditional BMI definition has been questioned. In recent years, groups like the Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology global commission have also argued that BMI alone is not enough. The problem with BMI is that it does not account for muscle mass or where fat is located on the body. For example, fat stored around the stomach is often considered more dangerous to health than fat stored in other areas. The EASO framework fixes this by including a measurement of waist-to-height ratio.
paragraphs.zh: 這並非傳統身體質量指數定義首次受到質疑。近年來，像是《刺胳針糖尿病與內分泌學》（Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology）全球委員會等組織也主張，單靠身體質量指數是不夠的。身體質量指數的問題在於它沒有將肌肉量或脂肪在身體的分佈位置納入考量。例如，堆積在腹部的脂肪通常被認為比堆積在其他部位的脂肪對健康更具危害。歐洲肥胖研究協會的架構透過納入腰高比的測量，解決了這個問題。

paragraphs.en: Despite these findings, the researchers acknowledge that there is still much to learn. While the link between the new obesity definition and dementia is clear, the exact reasons why some people develop these conditions while others do not remain a subject of ongoing study. The researchers hope that their work will encourage medical professionals to stop relying only on BMI and start looking at the full health profile of their patients.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些發現，研究人員仍承認還有許多未知之處。雖然新的肥胖定義與失智症之間的關聯已很明確，但為何有些人會罹患這些疾病而其他人不會，其確切原因仍是持續研究的課題。研究人員希望他們的工作能鼓勵醫療專業人員，停止僅依賴身體質量指數，並開始審視病患完整的健康概況。

paragraphs.en: As we look toward the future, these findings suggest a shift in how we approach preventative medicine. If doctors can identify who is at the highest risk for dementia using these broader criteria, they may be able to offer better advice on diet, exercise, and medical care. For now, the study serves as a strong reminder that health is complex. It is not just about a single number on a scale, but about how different parts of our body work together. As more data becomes available, the medical community will likely continue to move toward these more detailed and accurate ways of measuring health.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，這些發現顯示我們在預防醫學的處理方式上將有所轉變。如果醫師能利用這些更廣泛的標準，識別出誰是失智症的高風險群，或許就能提供關於飲食、運動與醫療照護更好的建議。目前而言，這項研究強烈提醒我們，健康是複雜的。它不僅僅是體重計上的一個數字，而是關於身體各個部位如何共同運作。隨著更多數據的取得，醫學界很可能會持續朝向這些更細緻、更精確的健康衡量方式邁進。

previousArticles.summaryEn: A new study suggests that the traditional way of measuring obesity is not enough to understand health risks. Researchers found that using a broader definition of obesity helps identify more people at risk of dementia. This new method looks at body fat, health conditions, and how fat is distributed on the body. The study compared data from thousands of people in England and China. Experts believe this approach could lead to better health outcomes in the future.

quiz.question: According to the article, what specific change occurs when the EASO framework is applied to people previously labeled as 'overweight'?

options.A: They are reclassified as having a normal weight.
options.B: More than 80% are reclassified into the 'obesity' category.
options.C: They are found to have no risk of developing dementia.
options.D: They are identified as having lower muscle mass than previously thought.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，研究人員應用 EASO 規則後，發現超過 80% 原本被標記為「過重」的人，實際上屬於「肥胖」類別。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章提到這類人反而可能面臨更高的失智風險；選項 D 雖然文章提到 BMI 不計算肌肉量，但並非此處提到的研究結果。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the limitations of using BMI as the sole indicator of health?

options.A: BMI is too expensive for most doctors to calculate during routine check-ups.
options.B: BMI fails to distinguish between different types of body composition and fat distribution.
options.C: BMI was originally designed to measure dementia risk rather than general health.
options.D: BMI is only accurate for people living in China and England.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第六段，文章提到 BMI 的問題在於它不考慮肌肉量或脂肪的儲存位置（如腹部脂肪較危險），因此它無法全面反映健康狀況。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 C 錯誤，BMI 是傳統健康衡量方式；選項 D 錯誤，研究樣本來自兩國，但並未暗示 BMI 的準確性僅限於這些地區。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does the word 'comorbidities' refer to?

options.A: The physical act of measuring height and weight.
options.B: The specific type of fat stored around the stomach.
options.C: The presence of multiple medical conditions in one person simultaneously.
options.D: The psychological stress caused by a diagnosis of dementia.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第二段明確定義了 comorbidities 為「the presence of two or more diseases in the same person at the same time」，即共病症。選項 A、B、D 皆與該醫學術語的定義不符，屬於對詞彙的錯誤理解。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: Obesity is the only factor that causes dementia in older adults.
options.B: The EASO framework is the only reliable way to measure human weight.
options.C: Modern medicine should move beyond simple BMI calculations to a more comprehensive health assessment.
options.D: People who are overweight should stop using BMI and focus entirely on their waist-to-height ratio.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心主旨在於探討為何 BMI 不再足夠，並強調醫學界應採用如 EASO 系統般更全面、細緻的健康評估方式，以更準確地預測疾病風險。選項 A 太過絕對；選項 B 誇大了 EASO 的唯一性；選項 D 建議過於狹隘，未涵蓋文章強調的整體健康概況。
